text:
Brindle Systems Unveils Compact Smart Meter

Brindle Systems, a Manchester-based maker of energy equipment, yesterday launched the Aura 3, a smart meter that it says can [1] household electricity use in real time without a separate display unit. The device, which goes on sale in March, transmits data to a smartphone application over an encrypted connection.

Analysts had expected the product to cost more than £80. [2], the company has priced it at £59, a decision that chief executive Hana Petrova attributed to lower manufacturing costs. [3] Evidence of this broader appeal is already apparent: two regional suppliers are reported to be negotiating bulk orders.

Consumer groups have welcomed the price but warned that the meter, [4] to work only with newer smartphones, may exclude some older users.

questions.explanation: A meter that works 'in real time without a separate display unit' measures and tracks use, so 'monitor' fits. 'curb', 'ration' and 'conserve' describe actively reducing consumption, which a meter does not do by itself.

Analysts expected a price above £80, but the company 'has priced it at £59': 'Instead' marks the replacement of the expected outcome. 'Likewise' and 'Moreover' add or compare, and 'Hence' would make the low price a result of the expectation.

choices: The lower price is expected to widen the product's appeal beyond early adopters of home technology.
The lower price is likely to reduce the company's profit margin on each unit sold in the first year.
The lower price is expected to attract criticism from rival makers whose devices sell at a premium.
The higher price is expected to limit the product's appeal to early adopters of home technology.
questions.explanation: 'this broader appeal' needs an antecedent about wider appeal, which only the correct sentence gives, and the bulk orders are the evidence. The 'higher price' contradicts the £59 figure and speaks of limited appeal, while the sentences about rival criticism and profit margins never mention appeal.

'the meter, designed to work only with newer smartphones' is a reduced passive clause: the meter is designed by the company. 'designing' and 'having designed' are active, and 'to design' cannot follow the noun in this way.

text:
To: Export Documentation Team
From: Henrik Aalto, Customs Compliance Manager
Subject: Revised procedure for certificates of origin

Effective 1 February, every export consignment bound for the Mercosur region must be accompanied by a certificate of origin [1] by the Chamber of Commerce. [2] As a result, the company incurred storage charges of more than €6,000 and strained relations with two long-standing customers.

To avoid a repetition, each declaration will be reviewed by a second team member before it is submitted. [3], no declaration may be filed without a checklist signed by both reviewers. Any discrepancy must be [4] to the compliance office within 24 hours.

Details of the revised checklist are attached. A training session for all declaration clerks will be held in the main conference room on 20 January; attendance is compulsory.

questions.explanation: The past participle 'stamped' forms a reduced passive clause: the certificate is stamped by the Chamber of Commerce. 'stamping' and 'to stamp' are active, and 'stamps' cannot follow the noun phrase.

choices: Several shipments cleared customs at the port of Santos within a day thanks to their prior stamping.
Several shipments were released at the port of Santos last quarter despite the absence of the required stamps.
Several shipments will be held at the port of Santos next quarter unless stamps are supplied.
Several shipments were held up at the port of Santos last quarter because of the missing stamps.
questions.explanation: 'As a result, the company incurred storage charges' needs a past event that caused delay, namely the shipments 'held ... because of missing' stamps. 'released ... despite' and 'cleared customs ... within a day' cause no delay, and 'will be held ... next quarter' is future, so 'incurred' could not follow it.

The sentence adds a further control to the review by a colleague, so 'Moreover' is correct. 'Nevertheless' and 'Instead' signal contrast or replacement, and 'Otherwise' means 'if not', which no condition in the memo supports.

'escalate' is the usual verb for referring a problem to a higher authority, as in 'escalated to the compliance office'. 'relegated' implies demotion, and 'advanced' and 'upgraded' do not collocate with 'discrepancy' in this sense.

text:
Sustainability Coordinator – Orrin & Vale Architects, Leeds

Orrin & Vale Architects, a design practice with 180 employees, has committed [1] net-zero operational emissions by 2030 and is seeking a Sustainability Coordinator to lead the programme. The successful candidate will report to the Managing Partner and work closely with the facilities, procurement and human resources teams. Responsibilities include compiling the annual carbon report, advising project teams on low-carbon materials and running staff engagement campaigns.

Applicants must hold a degree in environmental science. A professional qualification in energy management is not essential, [2] candidates demonstrate at least three years of experience in a corporate setting. Salary will be [3] with experience, and benefits include a generous pension contribution and flexible working arrangements.

Applications, comprising a CV and a covering letter, should be sent to careers@orrinvale.example by 30 January. [4]

questions.explanation: 'commit to' is followed by a gerund, so 'has committed to achieving' is correct. 'achieving' alone lacks the preposition, and 'for achieving' and 'on achieving' use a preposition that 'commit' does not take.
'provided that' sets the condition under which the qualification is waived: three years of experience. 'in case' and 'so that' express precaution and purpose, and 'unless' would reverse the meaning.
'commensurate with experience' is the standard phrase in job advertisements. 'comparable' and 'consistent' do not describe how a salary is set, and 'proportionate' is normally followed by 'to'.

choices: Shortlisted candidates were notified by 6 February and interviewed in Leeds during the following week.
Shortlisted candidates will be notified by 6 February and interviewed in Leeds during the following week.
Shortlisted candidates will be notified by 6 February and interviewed in Leeds during the previous week.
Shortlisted candidates will be notified by 20 January and interviewed in Leeds during the following week.
questions.explanation: Applications close on '30 January', so notification on 6 February followed by interviews 'during the following week' respects the sequence. 'by 20 January' falls before the deadline, 'were notified' uses the past tense for a future process, and interviews 'during the previous week' would come before the candidates are notified.

text:
Preparing for Your Annual Audit – Kestrel & Moore LLP

An audit is far more than a check of figures; it is an independent examination that enables us to [1] whether your financial statements give a true and fair view of your company's position. [2] Our teams therefore begin each engagement by reviewing the controls that govern how transactions are recorded.

Fieldwork typically starts six weeks after the year-end and lasts two to three weeks; [3], it may take considerably longer where records are incomplete. To avoid delays, please ensure that bank statements, loan agreements and supplier ledgers are available on the first day. [4] significant discrepancies come to light, we will inform your finance director without delay.

The draft report will be issued within ten working days of the end of fieldwork, and management will then have a further ten working days to comment before it is finalized.

questions.explanation: 'determine whether' introduces the judgement the auditor must reach about the statements. 'detect', 'derive' and 'defend' cannot take a 'whether' clause expressing an assessment.

choices: The reliability of any financial statement is guaranteed by the auditor's signature on the final report.
The reliability of any financial statement is rarely questioned by shareholders, who tend to trust published accounts.
The reliability of any financial statement cannot be assessed until the year has ended and the books are closed.
The reliability of any financial statement depends largely on the quality of the internal controls behind it.
questions.explanation: 'therefore begin ... by reviewing the controls' requires a reason, and reliance on 'the internal controls' is exactly that. Waiting for the year-end, shareholders' trust and a signature that 'guarantees' reliability do not explain why controls are reviewed first.

The sentence qualifies the typical 'two to three weeks' by saying the work 'may take considerably longer', which calls for a concessive connector, 'Nonetheless'. 'Accordingly' and 'Hence' express consequence, and 'Likewise' expresses similarity.

'Should significant discrepancies come to light' is a formal inverted conditional meaning 'if'. 'Were' needs 'to' and 'Had' needs a past participle, and 'Unless' would contradict the promise to inform the finance director.

text:
To: All Exhibitors
From: Sunniva Berg, Operations Manager
Subject: Stand build and load-in arrangements

Dear Exhibitors,

Thank you for confirming your participation in the Nordic Packaging Expo, which will take place at the Aurora Exhibition Centre from 14 to 16 May. I am writing to set out the arrangements for the build-up period. [1] To manage this volume of traffic, access to the halls will be permitted from 8 a.m. on 12 May [2] vehicles display a valid loading permit.

Each permit allows a maximum of ninety minutes at the loading bay, so we recommend that you schedule deliveries in advance. Stands exceeding three metres in height require prior approval from our technical team. [3] Late submissions cannot be processed, and the corresponding stands will be limited to the standard height.

Please confirm receipt of this message and let me know [4] you require additional loading permits.

Kind regards,
Sunniva Berg

choices: Our records indicate that approximately 140 freight vehicles will arrive during the build-up period.
Our records indicate that no freight vehicles will arrive at the centre before the morning of 13 May.
Our records indicate that approximately 140 visitors will attend the opening ceremony on 14 May.
Freight forwarders have asked that the build-up start on 11 May to ease pressure on the loading bay.
questions.explanation: 'this volume of traffic' needs a stated quantity of vehicles during the build-up, as the correct sentence gives. 'visitors ... on 14 May' is not build-up traffic, 'no freight vehicles ... before 13 May' conflicts with access from 12 May, and the forwarders' request mentions no volume.

Access is allowed on the condition that vehicles show a permit, which 'provided that' expresses. 'in case' means as a precaution, 'whereas' is a contrast, and 'even if' would make the permit irrelevant.

choices: Detailed drawings may be submitted through the exhibitor portal at any time before the opening day.
Detailed drawings submitted through the exhibitor portal will be returned to exhibitors by 25 April.
Detailed drawings are not required for any stand until the day before the exhibition opens.
Detailed drawings must be uploaded through the exhibitor portal no later than 25 April at midnight.
questions.explanation: 'Late submissions' implies a deadline, which only the sentence with 'no later than 25 April' sets. 'not required ... until the day before' and 'at any time before the opening day' set no deadline, and drawings 'returned ... by 25 April' describe a different step.
'let me know whether you require ...' needs a conjunction expressing a yes/no question, so 'whether' is correct. 'that', 'what' and 'which' do not fit before a clause that is already complete.
